draft.title: Discursive writing craft
card: A discursive piece explores an idea instead of arguing for one fixed position. The writer follows a line of thought and lets the reader watch it develop.
It often mixes anecdote with reflection. An anecdote is a short story from life. Reflection steps back and asks what that story suggests about the wider idea.
The writer can change their mind along the way. A doubt, a second view or a surprise can turn the thinking in a new direction.
Its interest lies in the quality of the thinking, not in a final verdict. It can end with a question or an open thought instead of a firm conclusion.
draft.remember: A discursive piece is about the journey of the thinking, and the writer may end up somewhere unexpected.

a.q: Which description best fits a discursive piece of writing?
opts: It follows a developing line of thought about an idea
It proves one fixed position with a list of facts
It retells a single event in strict time order
It explains the choices a writer made in a draft
a.why: A discursive piece explores an idea and lets the thinking develop, so the reader follows the writer's thought. The option about proving a fixed position describes a persuasive piece, which aims to win the reader over, while a discursive piece does not need a final verdict.
a.clue: Think about the thinking itself being the interest.

b.q: Nadia's piece opens with a story about her grandmother's garden in Orange. She reflects on what it taught her about patience, then doubts her own view when she recalls how restless she felt as a child. Which feature of discursive writing is shown by her doubt?
opts: The writer changes direction as the thinking develops
The writer states a final verdict for the reader
The writer uses an anecdote to open the piece
The writer repeats a phrase to build emphasis
b.why: Nadia questions her own earlier view, so the thinking turns in a new direction. That is a change of mind along the way. The anecdote is also a feature of discursive writing, but it is the opening story, not the doubt.
b.clue: Look at what she does after reflecting on patience.

a.best: It follows a developing line of thought about an idea

b.best: The writer changes direction as the thinking develops
